translation:
(Continuing Kadvun 1, Aad 6)

3. The Inscrutable One set his play afoot in Gokul -- a play that Brahma and the other gods long for. Hari himself touches all and yet is untouched by any of it.

4. Brahma, who carried off the calves, was left thwarted; the elder cowherd Hari is himself the maker of all. Hari, Hari -- in mere sport he fashions crores of universes.

Aad (opening) ||6||

1. The colour has taken, oh the colour has taken -- Lord, in meditation on Parabrahma; having looked at the path of rites, I have let it go.

2. It is not there, ah, it is not there -- what essence did I ever gain from it? No farther shore of worldly existence is to be seen.

3. The mind was steeped in love many a time before -- in son, in wife, in wealth, in youth.

4. All of that perishes, all of that perishes; every one of those pleasures is empty. Seeing this, the colour faded away.

Aad (opening) ||7||

1. Supreme Self, oh Supreme Self -- Lord, you are Parabrahma; you it was who created Brahma and Maheshwar.

2. You are your own, oh you are your own -- Lord, all this is yours in every age; now look to what is ours.

3. All of it, ah all of it -- in this fashion you spread yourself abroad; of your own self you became the Unmanifest.

4. You are the great one, oh you are the great one -- such is the support of the ages; if [your own] must suffer sorrow, does that not shame you?

Aad (opening) ||8||

Here the first Kadvun is complete ||1||

Here begins the second Kadvun ||2||

1. Hari, Hari -- Kanha, lord of crores of universes, the great king of the Yadavs; him the Vedas and Upanishads sing.

2. Hari, Hari -- the sages who worshipped him with oblations: the knowing ones he made unknowing; when he stood before them asking, only then was he recognised.

3. Hari, Hari -- the women recognised him as the Purusha of the sacrifice; the unknowing he made knowing, and to them he gave the supreme state.

4. Hari, Hari -- he gladdened his teacher Sandipani, that Lord who is a wondrous giver; from him the guru asked back his dead son [as his fee].

Aad (opening) ||1||

1. Hari lifted the hill of Govardhan upon his hand; he is the uplifter of the age -- remembrance of the endless God.

2. Hari it is who stirs the hearts of loving women, exceedingly beautiful; on him Dhruv, Shuk and Narad set their thought.

3. The gods stand at the gate of Hari's Vaikunth; though they gaze, they do not attain it; the great sages enter within.

4. Hari's saints, filled with bliss, sport in happiness; they follow close after him; theirs is the rule of the fearless realm.

Aad (opening) ||2||

1. Hari, Hari -- the company of the saints: keep that satsang (holy company) night and day, and drink the supreme bliss.

2. Birth and death depart, they depart; there is no fear of coming again into the world -- a place beyond the reach of gods, sages and Indra.

3. Take refuge in Hari -- he who releases the caged soul, the ocean of compassion, the giver of riches and of the imperishable state.

4. Hari, Hari -- Dhruv, Prahlad and Vibhishan he made unshakable; unmoving is his grace upon his devotees.

Aad (opening) ||3||

1. As fire is one, Lord, and from it many lamps are lit; the fire is exceedingly strong -- the lamp, Hari, has not that strength.

2. That fire is Parabrahma, Lord; the lamps are Hari, Har and Brahma, gods, men and serpents -- everything that stands still and everything that moves.

3. Great is he, the support of the ages, Lord, whose limit is never found; he who took sixteen thousand brides -- that Hari; and great are Brahma and Shankar.

4. Let the soul abide in meditation on Hari; Lord, do not take prakriti (material nature) to be your own self. Parabrahma is unmanifest; all that moves serves Hari.

5. The soul is in your hand, Lord; it does not belong with prakriti. Without Hari I have wandered through crores of births; now I have come to follow, taking refuge in Hari.

Aad (opening) ||4||

1. Having been born into a body, how can you ask for happiness? You are already in the hands of your enemies. The objects of sense do not release you for an instant; death walks beside you every moment.

2. Blind in the midst of the pleasures you live among -- brother, you are falling into ruin. In your folly you do not wake; you will suffer sorrow to the very end.

3. You alone were before creation; you, Hari, are the maker of all. You alone are great and all-capable; you, Hari, are the treasury of compassion.

4. To the servant who serves you, you are merciful; to the man without devotion you are Death itself. I am tormented, in the grip of karma and the senses; now set this wretched one free.

5. You are Krishna, Govind, Murari -- carry this soul across. You are Hari, Purushottam, Parabrahma, Vishnu, Narayan.

6. Dark as the rain-cloud, robed in yellow silk, endlessly lovely of form; lotus-eyed and lotus-faced, husband of the daughter of the lord of the waters [Lakshmi].

7. Those who came to him even in enmity -- their purpose too he accomplished. Those who followed him in the mood of bhakti (devotion) -- give them now the unshakable abode.

8. Spotless, inscrutable, incomparable -- no comparison for him can be spoken. Lord of the world, supreme God; meditate on that Ishwar night and day.

Aad (opening) ||5||

1. Devoted to his devotees, upholder of dharma -- that Hari is Nand's own child. Hari, Hari -- the enemies of the saints he ground down; Hari cast them from their place.

2. Ravan and the rest were set up by Har and the other gods, and Hari himself again set [his devotee] in that place; Hari is the support of his devotees.

3. In Vrindavan the support of the ages sports with the gopis, and is yet the true brahmachari (celibate); Hari is himself the master of the three worlds.

4. When the waters came flooding, he kept Gokul safe; Hari's play broke the rain-clouds apart; Hari is the giver of liberation.

Aad (opening) ||6||

1. The colour has taken, oh the colour has taken -- Lord, the fast crimson of madder; the fleeting safflower dye has washed away.

2. I have known it for poison, known it for poison -- the delight of lust that I found; all enjoyments are like fire.

3. Let it go now, let it go now -- I have found the world to be sorrow; dispassion I have embraced as my brother.

4. That has swept it away, that has swept it away -- I have seen through the fellowship of passion [unclear]; lust, anger and pride I have cast off.

Aad (opening) ||7||

1. Hari Govinda, oh Hari Govinda -- Lord, you are Parabrahma; begging your grace I make my prayer.

2. This little game, this little game -- set it aside now; in the power of others I have suffered sorrows.

3. This is our own, this is our own -- Lord, the very form of the Self; why then do you make them separate and set them rolling about?

4. You have spread yourself out, you have spread yourself out -- exceedingly clever and all-knowing; alone you sport within the four mines of birth.

Aad (opening) ||8||

Here the second Kadvun is complete ||2||
